name: Bean Anthracnose
description: A seed-borne fungal disease causing sunken dark lesions on bean stems, leaves, and pods. It is most severe in cool, wet conditions and can cause significant yield losses in susceptible varieties.
symptoms: Dark brown to black sunken lesions on cotyledons and stems of seedlings
Brown circular spots on leaves with dark borders
Veins on lower leaf surfaces turning dark
Pod lesions as circular or oval sunken spots with reddish-brown borders
Pink spore masses in lesion centers under humid conditions
causes: Seed-borne infection serving as primary inoculum
treatments: Apply fungicides containing chlorothalonil or mancozeb at first symptoms
Spray azoxystrobin or pyraclostrobin for systemic control
Use copper-based fungicides as preventive treatment
Remove and destroy infected plant parts
prevention: Treat seeds with fungicide before planting
Practice crop rotation with non-legume crops (3+ years)
Remove and destroy crop residue after harvest
